name: Avau
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog refs are only sociolinguistic surveys (Van Cott & Spencer 2015) and comparative Ross 1988; no phonology/grammar found

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1/5.3 reference list for avau1237 (6 refs: Ross 1988; Hoopert & Wakefield 1980; SIL surveys of Amio-Gelimi 2013, Bebeli 2013, Ambul 2011, Avau 2015) and Glottolog CLDF sources.bib a full-text search for stress/accent [avb]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No grammar, grammar sketch or phonology is registered for Avau (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology); no silpng-provider entry (i.e. no SIL-PNG Organised Phonology Data) is coded for [avb].

sources.citation: Sato, Hiroko. HS1 collection, Kaipuleohone (University of Hawai'i): Avau elicitation recordings HS1-331 (hdl:10125/54503) and HS1-360 (hdl:10125/54532) 'basic vocabulary of Avau', HS1-098 basic sentences (hdl:10125/36770).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No written description exists; these open-access audio recordings of isolated words are the only material from which Avau stress placement could be determined (instrumentally or by ear); also worth asking Sato whether an Avau/East Arawe sketch is in preparation.

sources.citation: Van Cott, Sara & Juliann Spencer. 2015. A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Avau Language Area, West New Britain Province. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2015-006. Dallas: SIL International. 79 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Appendix A 'Characteristics of the language' (pp. 28-30) gives only consonant and vowel phone charts (Tables 13-14), a list of 34 vowel sequences, and morphology/grammar notes; the words 'stress', 'accent', 'syllable', 'tone' do not occur anywhere in the report, and the Appendix C.1 Avau wordlists (six villages, SIL-PNG 190-item list, phonetic transcription) carry no stress marks.

sources.citation: MacKenzie, Bonnie, Juliann Spencer & Sara Van Cott. 2013. A Sociolinguistic Survey of Bebeli. SIL Electronic Survey Report. Dallas: SIL International. 96 pp. (and Spencer, Van Cott & MacKenzie 2013, A Sociolinguistic Survey of the Amio-Gelimi Language Area, 101 pp.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sister East Arawe languages surveyed by the same team with the same Appendix A template; would show whether any stress remark exists for the subgroup (none expected) and contain further Avau wordlists.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98. Canberra: ANU. (ch. 5, SW New Britain network, pp. 160-183)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988) (also lendable online at archive.org)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Nothing for Avau; Avau appears only in comparative sound-correspondence and morphology tables (pp. 161-167, 183). The only stress discussion in the book concerns Ali (Schouten chain), not New Britain.

sources.citation: Hoopert, Daniel A. & David C. Wakefield. 1980. The languages and communities of south-western New Britain. In R. L. Johnston (ed.), Language, communication and development in New Britain, 5-40. Ukarumpa: Summer Institute of Linguistics.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Only other first-hand linguistic notes on Avau (Aringring village data, pp. 13-22 grammatical information per Van Cott & Spencer 2015:30); SIL survey chapters of this era sometimes include a phonology paragraph with a stress remark.

sources.citation: Sato, Hiroko. 2015-2017.
